_comment: Lab 4 — dashboard as code. Portable Grafana definition; import it, or translate the panels to CloudWatch / Azure Monitor / Cloud Monitoring. Committing the dashboard is better than clicking one together, and is noted favourably.
title: ITCS355 — Prediction service

panels.title: Request rate
panels._note: Baseline for interpreting every other panel. A change in rate changes what the other numbers mean — a spike in latency during a traffic spike is different from a spike with steady traffic.

panels.title: Error rate by class
panels._note: 4xx and 5xx must be split. 4xx is usually a caller problem; 5xx is yours.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels._note: If p99 is far above p95 in a repeating pattern, suspect cold start or a per-request model load.

panels.title: Feature drift (PSI, rolling)
panels._note: PSI per feature, emitted from monitoring/drift.py via adapter.emit_metric(). Threshold lines: 0.10 (stable), 0.25 (significant). The panel alerts on drift_psi{feature=~".+"} > 0.25 for 1h.

panels.title: Model version in production
panels._note: During a canary you should see two. If you see two when you are not deploying, something is wrong.

panels.title: Drift alert history
panels._note: How many drift alerts fired in the last 24h, by feature. A row of zeros is the healthy default; a sudden count is the signal to look at panel 4.

alerting._comment: Panel 4 thresholds trigger an alert when any feature's PSI exceeds 0.25 for 5 minutes.

annotations.runbook: Before retraining, check whether the schema or null rate changed first — that indicates an upstream pipeline break, not data drift. See docs/postmortem-template.md.
